source_user: A team wants lower serving cost through weight-only quantization. Define a fair comparison. Scenario variant 141: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: fix model and prompts; compare quality, memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, kernel support, calibration set, and failure cases; report confidence intervals.
corrected_answer: Assume the same checkpoint, tokenizer, request trace, prompt and output-length distributions, decoding settings, serving stack, scheduler, hardware, drivers, power and thermal state are used for both arms; change only weight precision. Keep activation and KV-cache precision fixed and record bit width, group size, scale/outlier handling, calibration data provenance, held-out separation, kernel choice and fallback behavior. Define the estimand before testing as fully loaded cost per successful output token at each declared concurrency, not merely device memory saved. For scenario variant 141, test the falsifiable hypothesis that quantization lowers that cost while meeting pre-registered held-out quality, safety, correctness, TTFT and TPOT gates; reject it if the planned confidence interval fails to support the target reduction or any hard gate fails. After identical warm-up and compilation, run repeated randomized interleaved paired baseline/treatment trials on disjoint calibration and held-out workloads. Predeclare scoring rules, thresholds, sample size, stopping rule and confidence-interval method. Measure quality, safety and correctness; model and peak memory in GiB; TTFT and TPOT in ms/token; throughput in tokens/s; concurrency and utilization; errors, retries, timeouts, OOMs, kernel/fallback frequency and cleanup failures, with p50/p95/p99 and denominators. Log prompt mix, batching, cache state, compile status, temperature, power and cost inputs. Stratify or randomize request length, batch shape, replica placement, thermal state and kernel path; report measured facts separately from estimates and investigate missing data. Use only authorized, bounded canaries: gate rollout on all quality/safety/correctness and service SLO checks, retain the baseline, stop on error/latency/quality regressions, and roll back to the unchanged baseline on a tested signal. Do not claim a savings without the held-out paired results and expert review; redact sensitive traces and document evidence still required.
risks: Quantization may reduce quality or safety while improving cost; held-out gates can reveal unacceptable regressions.
Kernel fallbacks, batching, cache state, thermal throttling, or placement can confound latency and throughput comparisons.
Incomplete denominators or cost accounting can make apparent savings non-reproducible; traces and identifiers require redaction.
